title: Commitment Matrix and Backstop Policies for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a clear, quantifiable Commitment Matrix that maps hosted endpoints and cataloged model variants to commitment tranches (Guaranteed, Best-Effort, Experimental) and define backstop policies for capacity, quality regressions, and cross-region failover. This ticket consolidates PM/Eng/Infra input into a single playbook that productizes how we promise latency/throughput and what automatic mitigations run when commitments are at risk.
acceptance_criteria: A single Commitment Matrix spreadsheet exists (Confluence & Drive) mapping every hosted endpoint + model variant to a tranche and associated SLO/throughput targets.
Backstop policy catalogue documented with automated actions for: model fallback, region routing, reserved capacity activation, and cost-throttle thresholds.
Canary cadence and gating checklist defined and linked to the console rollout UI and release automation.
A dashboard for tranche-level health (latency, error rate, capacity headroom) is live in Grafana and linked on the playbook.
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime, Infra, and Customer Success recorded in Confluence.
Rollout runbook with post-mortem templates and owner assignments is published.
updates: 2025-01-21: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and sales engineering. Agreed on three commitment tranches: Guaranteed, Best-Effort, Experimental.
2025-01-27: Draft Commitment Matrix uploaded to Drive (drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/CM-2025-01). Runtime team provided initial throughput estimates for top 12 models.
2025-01-30: Engineering flagged a risk: current autoscaler lacks soft-priority preemption needed for Guaranteed tranche. Created ENG-22018 to track autoscaler prioritization changes.
2025-02-02: Design mocked a console affordance for tranche labels and a 'backstop activated' banner. DES-4102 created for UX polish and accessibility.

2025-02-04: Reviewed with Head of Product. Decision to include explicit cost budget caps per tranche and soft-fallback to quantized model variants when cost threshold exceeded. Action: integrate cost guardrails with billing alerts (PM-86933).
decisions: Define three commitment tranches: Guaranteed (SLA-backed latency/throughput), Best-Effort (observability + burst guarantees), Experimental (no guarantees, may be evicted under pressure).

Backstop actions prioritized: 1) automatic variant fallback (same model, lower precision/quantized), 2) regional reroute to lower latency region if capacity available, 3) engage reserved pool and finally 4) apply cost-throttle for low-priority traffic.
Canary window for tranche changes set to 48 hours for new code/model rollouts with automated rollback trigger at >5% latency or >3x error-rate change vs baseline.
Cost governors to be implemented as soft limits tied to per-customer monthly budget; emergency override requires Director sign-off recorded in an audit log.
risks: Autoscaler capability gap could delay Guaranteed tranche enforcement (dependency ENG-22018).
Quantized fallbacks may introduce regressions in quality for some prompt families; requires pre-release evals and prompt-set gating.
Cross-region routing increases egress costs and regulatory complexity for some enterprise customers in controlled regions.
If dashboards lag, on-call may not detect tranche breaches quickly; need end-to-end alerting test during rollout.
checklist: Align SLOs with legal for Guaranteed tranche SLA language
Create console banner + UX for backstop status (DES)
Instrument tranche-level alerts and run synthetic breach test
Publish playbook and collect stakeholder sign-offs
